title: LLMs Are Not Good Strategists, Yet Memory-Enhanced Agency Boosts Reasoning
abstract: arXiv:2608.12626v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Strategic reasoning in Large Language Models (LLMs) within long-horizon environments is often limited by inconsistent subgoals. In these settings, finite attention resources prevent the model from maintaining strategic coherence over thousands of steps. This limitation leads to strategic drift, where localized decisions fail to sustain a coherent trajectory across reasoning. To address this, we introduce EpicStar, a framework that enables agents to learn memory as policy to tackle long-horizon reasoning. Specifically, the agent maintains a bank of successful past episodes as a heuristic alongside a working memory to track short-term environmental changes. During inference, a dynamic gating mechanism determines whether to execute a retrieved action directly or to perform new reasoning through a contextual fusion of the retrieved episodes and current working memory. translated_title: 大语言模型并非优秀策略家，但增强记忆的代理机制能提升推理能力
translated_abstract: 在长时程环境中，大语言模型（LLMs）的策略推理常常受到不一致的子目标限制。在这些场景下，有限的注意力资源使模型难以在数千步内保持策略连贯性。这种限制导致了“策略漂移”，即局部决策无法维持跨推理的连贯轨迹。为解决这一问题，我们引入了EpicStar框架，该框架使代理能够将记忆作为策略来学习，以应对长时程推理挑战。具体而言，代理维护一个成功历史片段的库作为启发式信息，同时结合工作记忆来跟踪短期环境变化。在推理过程中，动态门控机制决定是直接执行检索到的动作，还是通过检索片段与当前工作记忆的上下文融合来进行新的推理。以《星际争霸II》为测试平台，我们将EpicStar与多种基线方法进行了对比评估。
tldr: EpicStar框架通过将记忆作为策略并引入动态门控机制，有效解决了大语言模型在长时程推理中的策略漂移问题，显著提升了策略连贯性。
en_tdlr: EpicStar framework addresses strategic drift in LLMs for long-horizon reasoning by learning memory as policy with a dynamic gating mechanism, enhancing strategic coherence.
